title: Encapsulate Customer Order Aggregates
description_markdown: From a simulated view combining `customers` and `orders`, retrieve `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`, `COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count`, and `COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS total_spent`. Group by `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`. Filter for `order_count >= 1`. Order by `total_spent` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Virtual view query
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 1 ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Models an analytical reporting view joining master profiles to order history.
hints: Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 1 ORDER BY total_spent DESC, c.customer_id ASC;

title: Virtual Student Grade Point Transcript
description_markdown: Construct an academic transcript view query: join `students` with `enrollments` and `marks`. For each student, compute `s.first_name`, `s.major`, count of assessments taken (`COUNT(m.mark_id)` as `assessments_count`), and average score (`ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2)` as `average_score`). Group by `s.student_id`, `s.first_name`, `s.major`. Order by `average_score` DESC, `s.student_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Virtual academic transcript
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT s.first_name, s.major, COUNT(m.mark_id) AS assessments_count, ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) AS average_score FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.major ORDER BY average_score DESC, s.student_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Encapsulates complex academic relationships into a single reporting relation.
hints: Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT s.first_name, s.major, COUNT(m.mark_id) AS assessments_count, ROUND(AVG(m.score), 2) AS average_score FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.major ORDER BY average_score DESC, s.student_id ASC;

title: Virtual Department Headcount and Payroll Summary
description_markdown: Create a view query aggregating payroll by department: join `departments d` and `employees e` on `d.dept_id = e.dept_id`. Return `d.dept_id`, `d.dept_name`, `COUNT(e.emp_id) AS total_staff`, and `ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary`. Group by `d.dept_id`, `d.dept_name`. Order by `avg_salary` DESC, `d.dept_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Department payroll summary view
SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS total_staff, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary
FROM departments d
JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name
ORDER BY avg_salary DESC, d.dept_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS total_staff, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC, d.dept_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Consolidates department headcount and average compensation metrics into a reusable reporting view.
common_mistakes: Omitting d.dept_name from the GROUP BY clause.
interview_tip: Aggregating views provide pre-built reporting metrics while keeping raw employee tables private.
hints: Aggregate with `COUNT(e.emp_id) AS total_staff` and `ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary`.

Query: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS total_staff, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC, d.dept_id ASC;
